title: HTMLFormElement.requestSubmit should allow specifying form overrides like a submit button does

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

I have a custom element that wants to submit a parent form while overriding the action or method. If I were submitting from the light DOM my submit button would include a formaction or formmethod attribute, but that doesn't work in the Shadow DOM. Instead, I'm calling form.requestSubmit from my form-associated custom element, but it doesn't give me a way to override the method or action.

### What solutions exist today?

Some ideas I've seen:

- Set the action and method properties temporarily and reset them after the submit.
- Add a hidden submit button in the light DOM

Both of these options seem pretty janky to me.

### How would you solve it?

I would add a new signature to HTMLFormElement.requestSubmit that allows all of the overrides that are available to a submit button.

### Anything else?

There is a gap in this proposal that is actually important to me: it doesn't provide for a declarative approach to the same behavior. I love the style encapsulation of Shadow DOM, but it would be great to make submit buttons that just work like submit buttons in a declarative way without a bunch of JavaScript. All form elements need a declarative story for participating in forms in the light DOM in my opinion, but this is addressed elsewhere in other issues.
